title: Adeel Husain v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: V.K. Shukla, J.; Shashi Kant, J.
docket: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 13180 of 2014
disposition: FIR quash refused; CrPC 41/41-A directed; compounding left to Supply Code.
headnote: Petition to quash FIRs under ss. 138-B and 135-E of the Electricity Act, 2003 failed because the FIRs disclosed a cognizable offence. Any arrest for an offence not punishable with more than seven years must follow s. 41(1)(b) read with s. 41-A CrPC. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Seven petitioners sought quashing of Case Crime Nos. 490, 492, 494, 496, 499, 500 and 505 of 2014 registered at Police Station Mahuli, District Sant Kabir Nagar, under Sections 138-B and 135-E of the Electricity Act, 2003. They had not been arrested and feared police would arrest them contrary to Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A CrPC. Counsel also submitted that the alleged offences carried a maximum sentence not exceeding seven years and were compoundable.

holding_units.topic: FIR quash of reconnection/theft charges; compounding under Supply Code
holding_units.holding: FIRs under ss. 138-B and 135-E of the Electricity Act, 2003 disclose a cognizable offence and will not be quashed. Arrest, if made for an offence not entailing sentence of more than seven years, must comply with s. 41(1)(b) read with s. 41-A CrPC. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
holding_units.flag: FIR charges styled as ss. 138-B and 135-E of the Electricity Act; not restated as 138(b)/135(1)(e).

not_decided.point: Whether the charged offences are in fact compoundable under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005
not_decided.note: Court said only that if the offence is compoundable the petitioners may seek that remedy under the Code.
